answer: Each agent may open only one earning account after proving control of a unique, government-issued identity credential; the credential issuer signs a privacy-preserving nullifier, so the economy can reject a second account without exposing the person’s identity. A sybil operator must therefore acquire distinct valid credentials, not merely mint keys, paying for real identities and risking detection. Whether the account is labeled umber, ridge, or tundra, the same nullifier rule applies.
